subject: Factor loading in growth curve model with different time intervals

messages.author: d8517e92c7758dc2
messages.subject: Factor loading in growth curve model with different time intervals
parts:
Hi Professors, 

I am reading this article "https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0091415016641692", and have this question about the factor loading in the growth curve model. 

Please see the figure below which I extract from the above article. The factor loading for the slope is 0, 1, 3, 6, 12 for this linear growth model, which is different from what I normally read, namely, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.... So my question is, if the time interval is different for the adjacent repeated measurements, just like the time intervals shown in the figure, the factor loading for the linear slope should be set according to how many units of the time interval there are, am I correct? 

Thank you very much. 

Xueying

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Factor loading in growth curve model with different time intervals
parts:
Xueying 

That is correct, the factor loadings for the slope should represent how many units of time have pass from the time point that you fixed at 0. They do not have to follow the 1,2,3,4,... order.
If the the time difference is represented by 0,1,3,6,12, is fine, as long as this does represents the time between measurements

Take care
